title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: When you one-hot encode a categorical variable, each category becomes a separate column with binary values (0 or 1).

title: Columns in the Design Matrix
text: The dataset has two categorical variables: 'sex' and $$'embark_{town'}$$. After one-hot encoding, how many columns will each variable contribute to the design matrix?

title: One-Hot Encoding 'sex'
text: The 'sex' column has two categories: 'male' and 'female'. One-hot encoding this column will result in two new columns.

title: One-Hot Encoding $$'embark_{town'}$$
text: The $$'embark_{town'}$$ column has five categories: 'Southampton', 'Cherbourg', 'Queenstown', 'London', and 'Oxford'. One-hot encoding this column will result in five new columns.

title: Total Columns in the Design Matrix
text: After one-hot encoding 'sex' and $$'embark_{town'}$$, the design matrix will have $$2$$ (for 'sex') + $$5$$ (for 'embark_town') $$=$$ $$7$$ columns.

title: Invertibility of a Matrix
text: A matrix is invertible if it is square and has full rank. The rank of a matrix is the number of linearly independent columns.

title: Checking Full Rank
text: To check if the matrix is full rank, ensure that the columns are linearly independent. If any column can be expressed as a linear combination of others, the matrix is not full rank.

title: Determine Invertibility
text: Given that the design matrix has $$7$$ columns, is it possible for it to be full rank with only $$20$$ rows?
